A1.justification: Both complete 17-page PDFs describe the same LOADS research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, neuron-activation analyses, cross-lingual evaluations and supplementary analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds topic-classification experiments, baseline comparisons and LOADS label-transferability findings.

M1.justification: The LOADS procedure remains unchanged: construct candidate label sets, average last-decoder-layer activation kurtosis over validation examples, and select the lowest-kurtosis set. v1 Section 6.1 and v2 Section 5.1 describe the same algorithm; the new comparators are evaluation baselines.

E1.justification: v2 adds topic classification using AG News and a three-topic subset of TweetTopic, substantially extending evaluation beyond stance classification. The nine English stance datasets and French/Portuguese RumourEval evaluations are retained.

E2.justification: v1 Table 5 compares LOADS only with original dataset labels. v2 Table 4 additionally evaluates Original + Verbalizer and Self-generated label words across the retained five models and stance datasets, as well as the new topic datasets.

E3.justification: The principal evaluation retains greedy decoding, macro-F1/wF2 and selection using 100 validation examples. Added topic experiments introduce specific splits and candidate-pool settings, including sampling 50 of 160 AG News combinations. The transfer analysis also changes from top-k performance-ranked sets to individual LOADS-selected sets. These are localized protocol additions and revisions.

E4.justification: v1 Section 4.2 and Appendix H analyze overlaps among performance-ranked best/worst labels across datasets and models. v2 replaces this substantial analysis with LOADS-selected label transferability in Section 5.3 and removes the original overlap heatmaps. Decoding, elaboration, prompt-sensitivity, data-efficiency and layer-wise analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use label-set performance variances, Spearman correlations with significance reporting, and paired chi-squared significance annotations for the main comparisons. v2 extends these practices to additional results without introducing new seed counts, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds topic correlations and classification scores, two baselines' results, and LOADS-selection overlap findings. For example, Table 4 reports Flan-T5-xl LOADS/original scores of 0.8530/0.8071 on TweetTopic and 0.8556/0.9209 on AG News. Matched stance, cross-lingual and retained appendix table values are unchanged; the old performance-ranked overlap results are removed.

T1.justification: The FFN formulation and kurtosis definition in Equations 1–2 are unchanged. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs. The revised transfer analysis changes an empirical procedure and interpretation rather than introducing new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: v2 broadens the introduction's main contribution claims to include topic classification and potentially transferring LOADS-selected labels across related datasets without collecting target-dataset samples. v1's contributions emphasize stance-based evidence, model generality and cross-lingual transfer. The central LOADS proposal remains the same.

C2.justification: Using its revised selection criterion, v2 argues that LOADS-selected labels are primarily model-dependent and transferable across datasets; v1 emphasized dataset and model dependence of performance-ranked labels. v2 also adds explanations for the new baselines' behavior, potential training-data leakage behind Flan-T5's AG News results, and an efficiency limitation for tasks with many classes.

D1.justification: Appendices A and C add topic-dataset access references, subset details and candidate-generation instructions, including TweetTopic subtopic synonyms and AG News combination sampling. Conversely, v1's disclosure that prompt templates were tuned on validation sets is removed; this does not establish that the underlying procedure changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds the TweetTopic and AG News source citations and explicitly distinguishes LOADS from prompt-tuning and verbalizer-based decoding. Most related-work coverage is retained. Consolidating the duplicate Kuzmin reference concerns the same cited work, rather than removing a research connection.

P1.justification: The abstract is substantially rewritten, Related Work moves from Section 7 to Section 2, and the former Sections 2–4 are reorganized into Section 3. LOADS evaluation and analysis receive clearer separate subsections, while the transferability narrative and limitations are substantially revised.

P2.justification: The main results table expands to include additional methods and task groups. Existing label-order plots are merged into appendix Figure 2, and elaboration tables are consolidated. The kurtosis scatterplot and two overlap figures are removed, while Table 1 is restructured into separate original/optimal-label columns. Retained plot images are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 makes LOADS easier to assess by adding two alternatives to the original-label baseline and testing a second classification task. Reporting mixed topic results and discussing potential training-data leakage also clarifies applicability. These are useful gains, but the removal of detailed performance-ranked overlap evidence and limited quantitative support for the broader dataset-transfer claim constrain the overall improvement.
